title: Teachable Review 2026: Is It Still the Best Platform to Sell Online Courses?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

**Last updated: June 7, 2026**

## Quick Answer

**Teachable** is one of the most popular all-in-one platforms for creating, marketing, and selling online courses. With over **150,000 creators** using it, more than **$10 billion earned** by its community, and **100 million+ students served** across 180 countries, it's a proven solution for anyone looking to build an education business. Plans start at **$29/month** (Starter, with a 7.5% transaction fee) and go up to **$139/month** (Growth, 0% fee). If you want a platform that handles everything — course creation, payment processing, student management, and affiliate marketing — without needing any technical skills, Teachable is the gold standard in 2026. However, the rising monthly fees and transaction costs on the Starter plan mean you should upgrade to Builder ($69/month) as soon as your revenue justifies it.

---

---

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Incredibly easy to use** — Drag-and-drop course builder, intuitive dashboard, zero technical skills required. You can have a course live in under an hour.
- **AI tools save massive time** — Generate course outlines, quizzes, subtitles, and translations in seconds with built-in AI. This alone can cut content creation time by 50%.
- **Built-in affiliate program** — Every plan (except Starter) includes affiliate marketing tools. Let others promote your courses and pay them a commission. It's the single best growth channel for course creators.
- **Great mobile experience** — iOS (4.6★ from 9,200+ ratings) and Android (4.3★ from 560+ reviews) apps mean your students can learn anywhere. Most competitors don't offer native mobile apps.
- **Flexible product types** — Sell online courses, coaching sessions, memberships, and digital downloads all from one platform. You're not limited to just courses.
- **Robust sales features** — Order bumps, upsells, coupons, abandoned cart recovery, and Buy Now, Pay Later (Klarna/Afterpay) help maximize revenue per student.
- **Global payment handling** — Automatic VAT and sales tax collection, multi-currency support, and payouts via Stripe and PayPal.
- **Drip content and certificates** — Schedule lessons to release over time and automatically generate completion certificates with your branding.

### Cons 👎

- **Transaction fees on Starter** — 7.5% per transaction is steep. You'll feel this on every sale until you upgrade to Builder ($69/month with 0% fee). If you're selling a $100 course, that's $7.50 per sale gone.
- **No built-in email marketing** — Teachable has basic email notifications but no proper email marketing tool. You'll need ConvertKit, Mailchimp, or ActiveCampaign for email sequences, adding $30-100/month to your costs.
- **Limited design customization** — Your school pages look good out of the box, but deep customization requires CSS/HTML knowledge. Compared to WordPress + LearnDash, you have less control over the look and feel.
- **Revenue cap on Starter** — Starter plan caps at $10K in revenue. Once you hit that, you're forced to upgrade. This feels restrictive for growing creators.
- **No native landing page builder** — You can't build high-converting sales pages with drag-and-drop. You'll need a separate tool like Carrd or Leadpages for sophisticated marketing funnels.
- **$10K revenue notification** — Some users report getting the "upgrade or your school will be suspended" notification even slightly below $10K, causing unnecessary stress.

---

## Who Is Teachable For?

**Teachable is perfect for:**
- **First-time course creators** who want the easiest possible start. The learning curve is practically flat.
- **Coaches and consultants** looking to package their expertise into online programs, memberships, or digital downloads.
- **Creators with existing audiences** (YouTube, email list, Instagram) who want to monetize without dealing with hosting, payment gateways, or technical setup.
- **Course businesses earning $1K-$50K/month** — the platform scales well at this range.

**Teachable is NOT ideal for:**
- **Enterprise teams** needing advanced compliance, SSO, custom roles, and white-glove onboarding (look at Thought Industries or LearnUpon).
- **Developers who want full design control** — WordPress with LearnDash or LifterLMS gives you total flexibility.
- **Ultra-budget creators** — if $29/month + 7.5% fees feels expensive, consider Thinkific's free plan or Podia's $39/month flat plan.

---

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### Course Creation & Student Experience

Teachable's course builder is famously simple. You upload videos, add text lessons, add quizzes, and organize everything into sections and lectures. The drag-and-drop interface is intuitive — anyone who's used a basic CMS can figure it out in minutes.

**Key course features:**
- **Video hosting** — Unlimited video uploads on all paid plans. Bandwidth is included. Videos are hosted on Teachable's CDN for fast streaming worldwide.
- **Drip content** — Release lessons on a schedule (e.g., Module 1 on day 1, Module 2 on day 7). This increases engagement and reduces overwhelm.
- **Quizzes & assignments** — Multiple choice, checkboxes, short answer, and file uploads. Auto-grading for quizzes, manual grading for assignments.
- **Completion certificates** — Automatically generated with your school name, course title, and student name. Customizable templates.
- **Discussion forums** — Per-lecture comments let students ask questions and interact. You can moderate and respond directly.
- **Mobile apps** — Students can learn offline (download lectures) via the Teachable iOS and Android apps. This is a significant differentiator — most competitors only offer mobile-responsive web, not native apps.

### AI Features (New in 2025-2026)

Teachable has invested heavily in AI tools, and it shows. The AI course outline generator can take a topic like "Watercolor Painting for Beginners" and produce a full curriculum in 5-10 seconds. The quiz generator creates in-depth assessments from your content. AI subtitles and translations (available on Growth plan and above) automatically transcribe your videos into multiple languages — Spanish, French, German, Japanese, and more.

**What works well:** The course outline generator is genuinely useful for overcoming the blank page problem. Starting with a solid outline and tweaking it is much faster than building from scratch.

**What needs improvement:** AI-generated quizzes sometimes create questions that are too generic. You'll want to review and customize them before publishing. The translations are good but not perfect — consider them a starting point, not a finished product.

### Marketing & Sales Tools

Teachable provides a solid set of built-in marketing tools that eliminate the need for many third-party apps:

- **Order bumps & upsells** — During checkout, offer an additional product (e.g., a workbook for $19) to increase average order value. Teachable reports an average increase of $30 per order.
- **Coupons & promotions** — Create discount codes with start/end dates, percentage or fixed amounts, and usage limits. You can also run limited-time sales.
- **Affiliate program** — Recruit affiliates who promote your courses for a commission. You set the commission rate (percentage or fixed), provide affiliate links and creatives, and track everything in the dashboard. This is arguably Teachable's strongest marketing feature.
- **Abandoned cart recovery** — Automatically email prospects who start checkout but don't complete the purchase. This single feature can recover 10-15% of lost sales.
- **Student referrals** — Give existing students a unique referral link and reward them when their friends purchase.
- **SEO tools** — Custom title tags, meta descriptions, and URL structures help your course pages rank on Google.

### Payment Processing

Teachable handles everything payment-related behind the scenes:

- **Payment gateways** — Stripe and PayPal are pre-integrated. You don't need to set anything up beyond connecting your account.
- **Buy Now, Pay Later** — Klarna and Afterpay options reduce friction for students who can't pay upfront.
- **Tax handling** — Automatic VAT collection for EU customers and sales tax for US states. Teachable calculates, collects, and remits taxes (with additional fees for the filing service on higher plans).
- **Global payouts** — Receive payments in USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, and AUD. Pay out via PayPal, Stripe, or bank transfer.
- **Multi-currency pricing** — Set different prices for different currencies to optimize conversion.

### Integrations

Teachable integrates with the most popular tools in the creator ecosystem:

- **Email marketing** — ConvertKit, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, Drip. Sync student data and segment based on purchases.
- **Analytics** — Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, and custom JavaScript for tracking.
- **Zapier** — Connect to 3,000+ apps for custom workflows (e.g., "when a student enrolls, add them to a Slack channel").
- **CRM** — HubSpot integration for more advanced customer management.

**Missing integrations:** There's no native integration with Notion, Airtable, or popular LMS tools like Canvas or Blackboard. Zapier can bridge some gaps, but it adds complexity.

---

## Pricing: What Does Teachable Really Cost?

Teachable has four tiers, plus a Custom Enterprise plan. All prices shown are annual billing — monthly is roughly 22% more.

| Plan | Monthly (Annual) | Transaction Fee | Products | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Starter** | $29/mo | 7.5% | 5 | Beginners testing the waters |
| **Builder** | $69/mo | 0% | 10 | Growing creators with >$5K/mo revenue |
| **Growth** ⭐ | $139/mo | 0% | 50 | Serious education businesses |
| **Custom** | Contact Sales | Custom | Unlimited | High-volume enterprise (>$20K/yr) |

**The hidden costs to consider:**
- **Starter's 7.5% fee** — If you sell $20K/year in courses, that's $1,500 in fees. Upgrading to Builder saves you that in transaction fees alone while the $69/month ($828/year) cost is significantly lower.
- **Email marketing add-on** — $30-100/month for ConvertKit or ActiveCampaign if you want professional email sequences.
- **Payment processing fees** — Stripe/PayPal charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction regardless of your Teachable plan. This is on top of Teachable's fees.
- **VAT filing service** — If you sell to EU customers, the automated VAT filing costs extra on lower plans.
- **Domain and hosting** — Teachable hosts your school on a subdomain (yourschool.teachable.com). A custom domain is included, but you'll need to buy it separately ($10-15/year).

**Pricing verdict:** The Growth plan at $139/month is the sweet spot for serious creators. The 0% transaction fee, 50 products, removed Teachable branding, and AI translation features justify the price. For absolute beginners, the Starter plan lets you validate your idea for $29/month before committing.

---

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose the Right Online Course Platform

Choosing a platform to sell online courses is one of the most important decisions you'll make as a digital creator. The wrong choice can cost you thousands in transaction fees, limit your growth, or lock you into a platform that doesn't fit your business model. Here are the key factors to evaluate.

### Transaction Fees vs. Monthly Subscription

This is the most misunderstood aspect of course platforms. A platform with a low monthly fee but high transaction fees (like Teachable Starter at $29/month + 7.5%) can end up costing more than a higher-priced platform with zero transaction fees once you hit a certain revenue threshold.

**The breakeven math is simple:** Teachable Starter ($29/month + 7.5%) vs. Builder ($69/month + 0%). At $533/month in course sales, the 7.5% fee equals $40 — exactly the price difference between Starter and Builder. So if you're making more than $533/month in sales, Builder is actually *cheaper* than Starter. Most creators don't realize this and stay on Starter too long, paying thousands in unnecessary fees.

### Mobile Experience for Students

If your audience learns on the go — and most do — a native mobile app is a must-have feature. Teachable is one of the few platforms that offers dedicated iOS and Android apps for students. This means your students can download lectures and watch them offline, receive push notifications, and have a smooth app-native experience. Most competitors (Thinkific, Podia, Kajabi) only offer mobile-responsive web, which is not the same thing.

### Marketing and Growth Features

Look for platforms that include affiliate marketing, order bumps, upsells, and abandoned cart recovery out of the box. These features directly impact your revenue and should be prioritized over flashy but less important features like custom themes or advanced analytics.

Teachable's affiliate program is particularly strong — you can recruit other creators to promote your courses on commission, turning your students into a sales force. This single feature has helped many creators reach six-figure revenues without spending a dollar on ads.

### Scalability

Your platform should grow with you. Teachable's tiered pricing means you start small and upgrade as you grow — but make sure the upgrade path is clear. The jump from Starter ($29/month) to Builder ($69/month) to Growth ($139/month) is reasonable, but the $10K revenue cap on Starter means you need to plan your upgrade proactively, not reactively.

### Integration Ecosystem

No platform does everything. You'll need email marketing (ConvertKit, Mailchimp), analytics (Google Analytics), and possibly CRM tools. Check that your chosen platform integrates with the tools you already use or plan to use. Teachable's Zapier integration makes it compatible with over 3,000 apps, but native integrations are always smoother than Zapier workflows.

---

## Teachable vs. Top Competitors

### Teachable vs. Kajabi

Kajabi is Teachable's closest direct competitor. Both are all-in-one platforms, but Kajabi includes email marketing and landing page builders natively. Kajabi's lowest plan is $149/month (no transaction fees), making it significantly more expensive than Teachable's Starter plan. However, if you factor in the cost of a separate email marketing tool ($30-100/month), the gap narrows.

**Winner depends on your needs:** If you want everything in one box and have the budget, Kajabi wins. If you prefer best-in-class tools for each function (Teachable + ConvertKit) or need a lower starting price, Teachable is better.

### Teachable vs. Thinkific

Thinkific is the main budget competitor. Its free plan supports 3 courses and unlimited students, and its Basic plan ($49/month) has 0% transaction fees. Thinkific also has a better built-in email system than Teachable. However, Thinkific's mobile experience is web-only (no native apps), its affiliate tools are less mature, and its design options are similarly limited. Teachable wins on student mobile experience and affiliate marketing features.

### Teachable vs. Podia

Podia is simpler and cheaper: $39/month flat with no transaction fees. It sells courses, memberships, and digital downloads. But Podia has fewer features — no quizzes, no certificates, no affiliate program, no native mobile apps. It's great for absolute beginners selling simple digital products, but Teachable is more powerful for serious education businesses.

### Teachable vs. Udemy

Udemy is a marketplace, not a platform. You don't build a school — you list your course alongside thousands of others. Udemy handles marketing but takes a massive cut (up to 63% on free-traffic sales). You also don't own your student email list. Teachable gives you full ownership of your audience, your data, and your brand. For most creators building a long-term business, Teachable is the superior choice.

### Teachable vs. Skillshare

Skillshare is another marketplace model. You earn royalties based on minutes watched rather than direct sales. This model works well for passive income from short-form educational content, but you have minimal control over pricing and no ownership of the student relationship. Teachable is the clear winner if you want to build a real business with recurring revenue, upsells, and a loyal customer base.

---

## Real-World Performance: What Creators Say

Teachable's mobile app consistently receives strong ratings:
- **iOS App Store**: 4.6/5 ⭐ from 9,293 ratings
- **Google Play**: 4.3/5 ⭐ from 563 reviews

Common praise includes: intuitive student interface, smooth video playback, easy purchase flow, and reliable download capabilities for offline learning.

Common complaints include: occasional app crashes after major iOS updates, limited discussion features, and slow load times on low-bandwidth connections.

On the creator side, Teachable's help center and community forums are highly regarded. The knowledge base is comprehensive, and most common questions have detailed walkthroughs. Live chat support is available on Builder and above with response times averaging 2-5 minutes.

---

## Tips for Getting the Most Out of Teachable

1. **Start on Starter, but plan your upgrade** — Use the free 7-day trial and the Starter plan to validate your course idea. Set a revenue goal (e.g., $3K/month) as your trigger to upgrade to Builder.
2. **Launch with an affiliate program from day one** — Recruit 10-20 micro-affiliates (bloggers, YouTubers, Instagrammers in your niche) before launch. Offer 30-50% commission. This is the fastest way to get initial sales.
3. **Use order bumps strategically** — Add a low-priced digital download ($9-19) to every checkout. Even a 20% conversion rate on a $15 bump adds significant monthly revenue.
4. **Set up abandoned cart recovery immediately** — This single setting recovers 10-15% of lost sales with zero ongoing effort.
5. **Drip your best content** — Don't release everything at once. Drip lessons over 4-6 weeks to keep students engaged and reduce refund requests.
6. **Pair Teachable with a real email tool** — Don't rely on Teachable's built-in notifications. Connect ConvertKit or Mailchimp for proper email sequences: welcome series, sales campaigns, and re-engagement emails.
7. **Review AI-generated content carefully** — The AI outline and quiz generators save time, but always review and customize before publishing. Generic AI content hurts your credibility.

---

## FAQ

### Is Teachable really free to start?

Teachable offers a 7-day free trial on all plans. After the trial, the lowest paid plan is Starter at $29/month (billed annually). There is no free forever plan like Thinkific offers. However, the 7-day trial is long enough to build and publish a complete course — just remember to set a reminder before the trial ends.

### Does Teachable take a percentage of my sales?

Yes, but it depends on your plan. Starter has a 7.5% transaction fee per sale. Builder and Growth have 0% transaction fees. On top of Teachable's fees, Stripe or PayPal take their standard 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. The 7.5% on Starter adds up quickly — if you sell $10K in courses annually, you pay $750 in transaction fees plus Stripe's cut.

### Can I use my own domain with Teachable?

Yes. All paid plans allow you to set a custom domain (e.g., courses.yourbusiness.com). You'll need to purchase the domain separately from a registrar like Namecheap or Google Domains, then follow Teachable's DNS configuration guide. It takes about 10-15 minutes to set up.

### Does Teachable offer email marketing?

Teachable has basic transactional email notifications (receipts, course enrollment confirmations) but no proper email marketing tool. You cannot create email sequences, newsletters, or automated campaigns within Teachable. You'll need to integrate with ConvertKit, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, or a similar email marketing platform.

### Is Teachable good for coaching and memberships?

Yes. Teachable now supports coaching products (one-on-one and group sessions with scheduling and payment management) and memberships (recurring subscriptions). This makes it a versatile platform for more than just courses — you can offer a complete suite of digital products from a single school.

### What payment methods do students have?

Students can pay via credit/debit card (powered by Stripe), PayPal, and Buy Now, Pay Later options (Klarna, Afterpay) depending on their region. All major currencies are supported. Teachable's checkout is mobile-optimized and designed for high conversion.

### Can I migrate from another platform to Teachable?

Teachable offers assisted migration on higher plans (Growth and Custom). For self-service migration, you can import students, courses (via CSV/API for basic data), and content. Most creators report that manual course rebuilding (uploading videos, writing lessons, setting up quizzes) is the most reliable approach for a clean transition.

### Does Teachable have a mobile app for creators?

Teachable does not have a dedicated creator-side mobile app to manage your school. The student apps (iOS and Android) are for learners only. To manage your school on the go, you use the mobile web version of the Teachable dashboard, which is functional but not as smooth as a native app.

### How does Teachable handle taxes?

Teachable automatically calculates and collects VAT for EU customers and sales tax for applicable US states. On Growth plan and above, they offer automated tax filing services. On Starter and Builder, you're responsible for remitting taxes to the relevant authorities. This is a critical consideration if you sell to international customers.

### What happens if my revenue exceeds the Starter plan cap?

Starter plan has a $10,000 revenue cap. Once you approach this limit, Teachable will notify you to upgrade to Builder. If you don't upgrade, your school may be suspended. The cap includes gross revenue (before fees and refunds), so it can sneak up on you faster than expected. Upgrade to Builder as soon as you consistently earn $3-5K/month to avoid disruption.

---

## Conclusion: Should You Use Teachable in 2026?

Teachable remains one of the best platforms for creating and selling online courses in 2026. Its ease of use, robust affiliate marketing tools, excellent mobile student experience, and new AI features make it a compelling choice for creators at every stage.

**Choose Teachable if:**
- You want the fastest path from idea to published course
- You plan to use affiliate marketing as your primary growth channel
- A mobile-first student experience matters to your audience
- You're comfortable with the monthly subscription model

**Skip Teachable if:**
- You need everything in one platform (including email marketing) — go with Kajabi
- You're on a very tight budget — try Thinkific's free plan
- You need deep customization and full design control — use WordPress + LearnDash

For most creators building a serious online education business, Teachable's combination of ease of use, powerful features, and proven track record is hard to beat. **Start with the 7-day free trial, build your first course, and upgrade from Starter to Builder as soon as your revenue justifies it.** The affiliate tools alone are worth the price of admission.

👉 **[Start your free Teachable trial here](https://teachable.com/)**
